details.Entry type: Team / method submission; not a verified model release
details.Submission description: We train neural networks with depth of over 150 layers for classification, detection, and segmentation. We propose a “deep residual learning” framework [a] that eases the optimization and convergence of extremely deep networks. Our “deep residual nets” enjoy accuracy gains when the networks are substantially deeper than those used previously. Such accuracy gains are not witnessed for many common networks when going deeper. Our instance semantic system is based on our work in [b]. We build a Multi-task Network Cascade for proposing regions, regressing masks, and categorizing instances. We develop an end-to-end algorithm for training this causal, cascaded system. In particular, we propose an “RoI warping” layer that is differentiable with respect to the region coordinates, so the entire backpropagation can be performed in a theoretically valid way. Our object detection system is based on the “Faster R-CNN” system in our NIPS paper [c]. The region proposal network (RPN) in Faster R-CNN effectively learns the proposals on the COCO dataset, and the result in this submission is obtained by using only 300 proposals per image for a single model. The object detection network is built based on the observations in [d]. Both object detection and instance segmentation systems benefit greatly from the extremely deep residual networks. On the COCO detection dataset, Faster R-CNN with a 101-layer residual net shows 30% relative improvement over the counterpart Faster R-CNN with VGG-16. The training set for the classification network is the 1000-class ImageNet training set. The training set for the detection task is the MS COCO trainval set with box-level annotations. The training set for the segmentation task is the MS COCO trainval set with mask-level annotations. [a] “Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition”, Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun. Tech Report 2015. [b] “Instance-aware semantic segmentation via multi-task network cascades”, Jifeng Dai, Kaiming He, Jian Sun. Tech Report 2015. [c] “Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks”, Shaoqing Ren, Kaiming He, Ross Girshick, Jian Sun. NIPS 2015. [d] “Object Detection Networks on Convolutional Feature Maps”, Shaoqing Ren, Kaiming He, Ross Girshick, Xiangyu Zhang, Jian Sun. arXiv 2015.

details.Submission description: We develop a novel region-based object detection and instance segmentation approach by boosting information flow from across layers, iterative pyramid and global context information. We use a feature pyramid Mask RCNN as our backbone [1, 2]. Our contributions are listed as follows. 1) Instead of assigning object proposals to different levels by a heuristic metric, we allow each proposal adaptively to pick useful information from all levels, leading to improved information flow from across layers. 2) We augment another path from lower layers to top layers based on the observation that larger objects could surprisingly benefit more from lower layer features, resulting in improved information flow from iterative pyramid. 3) We augment the FCN-like mask prediction branch with tiny fully-connected layers, improving information flow from global context information when predicting pixel-wise mask. As a result, masks with higher quality are produced. Our models are pre-trained on ImageNet and fine-tuned on COCO trainval subset with mask annotations. We directly take the tighten bounding boxes around each mask prediction as our object detection results. Our best single model performance is 44 in terms of instance segmentation and 47.8 in terms of object detection on test-dev subset. We find that the performances based on Resnext-101 (64*4d), SE-ResNext-101 (32*4d), Resnet-269 and SENet are just comparable. We hypothesis the reason is that the limited GPU memory makes the larger models can only be trained on smaller image input which limits their capability. For ensemble, we used 3 Resnext-101 (64*4d), 2 Se-ResNext-101 (32*4d), 1 Resnet-269 and 1 SENet. With network ensemble, we achieve 46.7 in terms of instance segmentation and 51 in terms of object detection on test-dev subset. [1] T. Lin, P. Dolla ́r, R. B. Girshick, K. He, B. Hariharan, and S. details.Submission description: We train neural networks with depth of over 150 layers for classification, detection, and segmentation. We propose a “deep residual learning” framework [a] that eases the optimization and convergence of extremely deep networks. Our “deep residual nets” enjoy accuracy gains when the networks are substantially deeper than those used previously. Such accuracy gains are not witnessed for many common networks when going deeper. Our instance semantic system is based on our work in [b]. We build a Multi-task Network Cascade for proposing regions, regressing masks, and categorizing instances. We develop an end-to-end algorithm for training this causal, cascaded system. In particular, we propose an “RoI warping” layer that is differentiable with respect to the region coordinates, so the entire backpropagation can be performed in a theoretically valid way. Our object detection system is based on the “Faster R-CNN” system in our NIPS paper [c]. The region proposal network (RPN) in Faster R-CNN effectively learns the proposals on the COCO dataset, and the result in this submission is obtained by using only 300 proposals per image for a single model. The object detection network is built based on the observations in [d]. Both object detection and instance segmentation systems benefit greatly from the extremely deep residual networks. On the COCO detection dataset, Faster R-CNN with a 101-layer residual net shows 30% relative improvement over the counterpart Faster R-CNN with VGG-16. The training set for the classification network is the 1000-class ImageNet training set. The training set for the detection task is the MS COCO trainval set with box-level annotations. The training set for the segmentation task is the MS COCO trainval set with mask-level annotations. [a] “Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition”, Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun. Tech Report 2015. [b] “Instance-aware semantic segmentation via multi-task network cascades”, Jifeng Dai, Kaiming He, Jian Sun. Tech Report 2015. [c] “Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks”, Shaoqing Ren, Kaiming He, Ross Girshick, Jian Sun. NIPS 2015. [d] “Object Detection Networks on Convolutional Feature Maps”, Shaoqing Ren, Kaiming He, Ross Girshick, Xiangyu Zhang, Jian Sun. arXiv 2015.

details.Submission description: We develop a novel region-based object detection and instance segmentation approach by boosting information flow from across layers, iterative pyramid and global context information. We use a feature pyramid Mask RCNN as our backbone [1, 2]. Our contributions are listed as follows. 1) Instead of assigning object proposals to different levels by a heuristic metric, we allow each proposal adaptively to pick useful information from all levels, leading to improved information flow from across layers. 2) We augment another path from lower layers to top layers based on the observation that larger objects could surprisingly benefit more from lower layer features, resulting in improved information flow from iterative pyramid. 3) We augment the FCN-like mask prediction branch with tiny fully-connected layers, improving information flow from global context information when predicting pixel-wise mask. As a result, masks with higher quality are produced. Our models are pre-trained on ImageNet and fine-tuned on COCO trainval subset with mask annotations. We directly take the tighten bounding boxes around each mask prediction as our object detection results. Our best single model performance is 44 in terms of instance segmentation and 47.8 in terms of object detection on test-dev subset. We find that the performances based on Resnext-101 (64*4d), SE-ResNext-101 (32*4d), Resnet-269 and SENet are just comparable. We hypothesis the reason is that the limited GPU memory makes the larger models can only be trained on smaller image input which limits their capability. For ensemble, we used 3 Resnext-101 (64*4d), 2 Se-ResNext-101 (32*4d), 1 Resnet-269 and 1 SENet. With network ensemble, we achieve 46.7 in terms of instance segmentation and 51 in terms of object detection on test-dev subset. [1] T. Lin, P. Dollár, R. B. Girshick, K. He, B. Hariharan, and S. J. details.Submission description: We develop a novel framework in this contest, which is distinguished from previous ones in three aspects: a new hybrid cascade architecture, a more intelligent anchoring scheme, and a new backbone network called FishNet. details.Submission description: In this challenge, we attempt to tackle the instance segmentation task with Mask RCNN based on a small batch size, i.e. 4. Since the small batch size would cause more unstable training and worse performance, we adopt several novel and effective techniques. First, we introduce group normalization [1] to stabilize the representation of CNN and use context refinement [2] to improve the accuracy of detected bounding boxes. Second, we try to alter the training statistics for different categories of objects because we find that the objects with fewer samples in the dataset generally have much worse performance. Since the small batch size cannot overcome this problem effectively, we introduce class re-sampling and class re-weighing strategies so that objects with fewer samples can also be trained adequately. The class re-sampling, which is similar to label smoothing, will sample more for the categories that have fewer objects in the dataset. The class re-weighing will then assign the objects that have a worse performance with higher weights in the loss function during training. Moreover, we introduce multi-scale training and crop training to boost robustness and accuracy. We also perform class-wise ensemble to augment the final performance. details.Submission description: The method makes instance segmentation and semantic segmentation predictions in a single network, and combines these outputs using heuristics to create a single panoptic segmentation output. The architecture consists of a ResNet-50 feature extractor shared by the semantic segmentation and instance segmentation branch. For instance segmentation, a Mask R-CNN type of architecture is used, while the semantic segmentation branch is augmented with a Pyramid Pooling Module. The feature extractor is initialized using weights from a model that is pre-trained on ImageNet. The network is trained on a single Titan Xp GPU, and the submitted results are from a single model.

details.Submission description: Based on the powerful FPN-Mask-RCNN [1,2] and Deeplabv3+ [3] model, we explore the possibility of combining the two models into a single e2e trainable model. When comparing the two models side by side, we can observe that both models share a similar “encoder-decoder” architecture that can be combined. In FPN-Mask-RCNN, the FPN backbone [1], which has an “encoder-decoder” architecture, can be used to create the Deeplabv3+ model. This is done by adding a FCN-style semantic prediction head onto the final feature-map of the pyramid structure. We reason that since each pyramid level contains information from the previous layer and also from the encoder branch through the skip connections, the final feature-map should contain the relevant information needed for pixel-wise semantic segmentation. In addition to the semantic head, we also incorporate the ASPP-layer from Deeplabv3+ into the FPN backbone. The model is then trained e2e (stably) using a combination of 6 losses: 5 losses from the standard Mask-RCNN and 1 from the semantic head. For the final panoptic segmentation, we employ only an adaptive thresholding method (AT-Fusion) to fuse the output predictions from the Mask-RCNN head and also the semantic prediction head. The fusion is done by first fusing the instances together using adaptive thresholding and prediction scores, while the semantic prediction is used to fill in the background. The adaptive thresholding is done by coupling the final thresholding of the instance detection with the prediction probability of the semantic head. There are 2 reasons for this adaptive thresholding. Firstly, compared to just using a certain region in the Mask-RCNN head, the semantic head uses the information from the entire image/scene for prediction, making the prediction much more reliable. Secondly, as “argmax” is used to produce the final semantic labels, a certain label doesn’t need to have a 0.99 prediction probability to be chosen as the final output. This means that if semantic prediction can be performed without hard constraint, then the same idea can also be applied to the instance detection. As of the time of submission, the first results are submitted for the challenge while experiments and works are still being done to validate the performance of the proposed method. [1] LIN, Tsung-Yi, et al. Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection. In: CVPR. 2017. S. 4. [2] HE, Kaiming, et al. Mask r-cnn. In: Computer Vision (ICCV), 2017 IEEE International Conference on. IEEE, 2017. S. 2980-2988. [3] CHEN, Liang-Chieh, et al. Encoder-decoder with atrous separable convolution for semantic image segmentation. arXiv preprint arXiv:1802.02611, 2018.
